title: Quintaster's Regrowing Spines
story: Quintaster the Cavern Urchin blocks the only exit from the crystal caves with 20 glowing spines. Snap off one spine and 4 new ones sprout in its place — but Mr 6 notices that each new spine is smaller and, more importantly, that Quintaster falls asleep the instant he has exactly 44 spines.
question: Starting at 20 spines, if each snap removes 1 spine and grows 4 new ones, how many snaps are needed to reach exactly 44 spines?
hint: Each snap changes the total by a net amount — you take one away and four appear. How much does the count go up per snap?
victory: On the eighth snap Quintaster hit 44 spines exactly and dozed off with a whistly snore, and Mr 6 tiptoed the whole caving party out past him.
imagePrompt: A giant spiny urchin creature glowing violet in a crystal cavern mouth, spines sprouting in bunches, as a numeral-six knight counts on his fingers with a sly grin.
solution: Each snap takes away 1 spine and adds 4, so the net gain is 4 - 1 = 3 spines per snap.
The spines need to grow from 20 to 44, which is 44 - 20 = 24 more spines.
praise: Tracking what happens on every snap was exactly the right instinct — the one missing step was combining the -1 and +4 into a net gain of 3.
